hyperedges.label: Unsigned build trust and verification chain

nodes.label: Release publish job (Tauri 2-platform matrix)
nodes.rationale: fail-fast:false matrix of windows-latest (nsis) and macos-latest (universal dmg); tauri-action creates the release as a draft (releaseDraft: true) so partial builds are never published automatically

nodes.label: Release checksums job (SHA256SUMS.txt)
nodes.rationale: Draft releases have no git tag ref yet, so /releases/tags/{tag} (used by gh release download/upload) 404s; the job resolves the release by id via the GitHub API instead, downloads every asset, and uploads SHA256SUMS.txt through the assets API

nodes.label: Release version gate (verify-release-version.mjs)
nodes.rationale: All version manifests (package.json, tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock) must agree and match the tag before a release build proceeds; package-lock.json is intentionally not gated

nodes.label: Verify native job (fmt, clippy, cargo test, no-bundle build)
nodes.rationale: Denied-warnings clippy and --locked cargo commands on a Windows/macOS matrix mirror the release matrix but build with --no-bundle; Linux legs are intentionally absent while Linux distribution is paused
nodes.norm_label: verify native job (fmt, clippy, cargo test, no-bundle build)

nodes.label: Saved HTML fixture parser tests
nodes.rationale: Saved HTML fixtures make parser tests deterministic and protect the WFMU parsers from accidental regressions; when WFMU changes its markup, fixtures and parser tests are updated together

nodes.label: Local-first architecture
nodes.rationale: No login, no cloud: all personal data (library, favourites, history, settings) stays in a local SQLite database in the OS app-data directory for org.archiplayer.app; nothing is synchronized or uploaded

nodes.label: WFMU polite cache-first fetch policy
nodes.rationale: WFMU exposes no official archive API, so Archiplayer parses public KenzoDB pages on demand at a strict one-request-per-second global rate, caches results instead of crawling, refreshes the A-Z index at most daily, refreshes a show page only after six hours, and offers no bulk audio download - to avoid burdening a listener-supported non-commercial station

nodes.label: Unsigned release builds
nodes.rationale: Community builds are unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper warn on open; users are told to verify the SHA-256 hash against SHA256SUMS.txt or build from source instead of trusting the binary blindly

nodes.label: Ignored live WFMU smoke test
nodes.rationale: Ignored by default because it performs live network requests against WFMU; run sparingly, only when working on the WFMU integration, and never in a loop

nodes.label: build-env.ps1 MSVC environment helper
nodes.rationale: Dot-sourced helper that selects stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, discovers Visual Studio Build Tools, and loads link.exe plus the Windows SDK into the shell without changing the rustup default

nodes.label: Tag-driven release process
nodes.rationale: Pushing a vX.Y.Z tag is the only correct release trigger; gh release create is forbidden because it creates the tag and pre-publishes a release that collides with what CI produces (this is how v0.3.0 got cut Windows-only by hand and had to be backfilled by CI)

nodes.label: Draft release review gate
nodes.rationale: Releases start as drafts and stay invisible to the website (which reads releases/latest, excluding drafts) until a human verifies all assets and publishes; if any platform leg fails, checksums is skipped and the partial draft must not be published

nodes.label: Release asset-name contract
nodes.rationale: site/site.js matches release assets by regex (Windows /setup.*\.exe$|\.msi$/i, macOS /\.dmg$/i, checksums /SHA256SUMS/i), so the build outputs must never be renamed or the site download buttons break; Linux has no matcher and is shown as coming soon

nodes.label: Repeatable-process reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Bundles are not byte-for-byte reproducible because NSIS and dmg embed timestamps and packaging metadata; reproducibility here means a repeatable process with pinned inputs (package-lock.json, Cargo.lock with --locked, Node 22, Rust stable, pinned actions) yielding functionally equivalent builds - byte-identical output is explicitly out of scope

nodes.label: scripts/release.ps1 one-command release
nodes.rationale: Automates check preconditions, version bump, version gate, release commit, push, confirmed tag push, CI watch, asset verification, and draft publish; the confirmation prompt before the tag push is the point of no return

nodes.label: Host-portable toolchain selection
nodes.rationale: src-tauri/rust-toolchain.toml stays on host-inferred stable while Windows helpers explicitly select stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc; this keeps macOS/Linux builds portable without letting a GNU-default Windows installation pick the wrong linker, and never forces a Windows-only toolchain on non-Windows hosts

nodes.label: Linux distribution pause
nodes.rationale: Linux distribution is paused and publicly marked coming soon while packaging, media playback, and compatibility are revalidated; Linux native and release CI jobs are intentionally absent, and issue #1 plus this PRD must be resumed before restoring Linux downloads

nodes.label: CSS variable sizing presets
nodes.rationale: Size/spacing presets (--icon-size, --pbtn-size, --pbtn-main-size, --pctl-gap, --player-gap) live once in :root next to the --c-* colour tokens so one edit applies globally, while the CSS cascade lets any element or modifier class override the same variable locally - nearest value wins

nodes.label: :global() icon piercing pattern
nodes.rationale: Svelte scoped CSS cannot reach into a child component's SVG, so a plain .pbtn.main svg selector does nothing; the pattern pierces with :global(svg.icon) kept under the scoped parent selector so it hits only that button

nodes.label: Archiplayer landing page (site/index.html)
nodes.rationale: Static GitHub Pages site with data-* hook attributes (data-asset, data-download-link, data-sha256-link, data-release-note, data-vt-todo) that site.js hydrates from the latest published GitHub release; includes SmartScreen/Gatekeeper guidance and a pre-launch VirusTotal placeholder
